subject: Re: ACME POC — evaluation plan, success criteria, and shadow vs offline methodology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME POC — post-call recap and next steps

Jordan — great conversation today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the POC kick-off: 

1) Success criteria (proposed):
   - Mean response latency under 700ms (95th pct under 1.2s) on target payloads
   - Answer accuracy >= 88% on the evaluation rubric (see attached)
   - Hallucination rate below 3% on the blind test set
   - Reasonable throughput to support your expected pilot traffic (20 req/s sustained)

2) Evaluation plan options (we discussed two approaches):
   A) Offline evals — run curated test prompts + holdout dataset; grade with rubric and automated metrics. Faster to iterate, good for quality gate.
   B) Online shadowing — mirror a subset of live traffic to Redwood in shadow mode; measure drift, latency, and recovery. Stronger signal for UX but needs sample traffic and consent.

3) Ownership / roles:
   - ACME: provide sample logs/datasets and target acceptance criteria (Sam/Jordan)
   - Redwood: provide eval rubric, run offline tests, set up shadow pipeline (Rachel to lead technical runbook)
   - Marissa: overall program owner and timeline coordination

4) Timeline (proposed):
   - This week: ACME shares sample dataset + pick acceptance metrics (by Fri 10/30)
   - Week of 11/2: Redwood runs baseline offline eval + shares first results
   - Week of 11/9: Optional 1-week shadow run (if ACME agrees)
   - Goal: decision on expansion by 11/20

Attachments: ACME-POC-Success-Criteria.xlsx, Eval-Rubric-v1.docx (attached)

Next step: Jordan — can you confirm who will own dataset deliverables and whether you prefer we start with offline-only or include a shadow run? I’ll schedule a short follow-up with Rachel to align on infra/permissions.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

---
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acme.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC — post-call recap and next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. Quick answers from our side: 

- I'll own the dataset entregar (Sam will help with access). We can provide a 10k-example holdout set and a 24-hour slice of anonymized production traffic for shadow if needed.
- We care most about accuracy and hallucination for the pilot; latency targets are important but can be relaxed a bit (95th < 1.5s acceptable).
- Prefer we start with the offline eval to set the baseline; we'll sign off on a short shadow run after seeing offline results.

I'll aim to upload the dataset to the drive link you shared by Friday 10/30. One question for Rachel: for shadowing, what minimal telemetry/permissions do you need from us?

—Jordan
Principal Product Manager, ACME Corp
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC — post-call recap and next steps

Jordan — thanks, that's perfect. Short answer on shadow telemetry and permissions:

- For a basic shadow run we need: request payload (anonymized), request timestamp, and the ground-truth label when available (or a human review process). No PII, please.
- We'll run the shadowed responses in a read-only mode; traffic is mirrored — no responses sent back to users. We only need network/config access to mirror to our collector endpoint (we provide a small collector script) or you can push log bundles to the shared Drive.
- We will capture latency, token counts, model confidence scores, and a per-response flag for hallucination/incorrectness based on the rubric.

On the rubric: attached Eval-Rubric-v1.docx is the scoring sheet we use. High-level grading buckets: Correct (2), Partially correct (1), Incorrect/hallucinated (0). We'll compute weighted accuracy and a hallucination rate. Example pass condition: weighted accuracy >= 0.88 AND hallucination rate <= 3%.

Proposed technical owners:
- Redwood: Rachel (eval infra, rubric application), infra team for collector script
- ACME: Jordan / Sam (data delivery, masking, minor infra changes)

Let me know if ACME wants us to run an initial offline pass on the data as-is or whether you'd prefer we wait until we have the production slice. We can do both — offline baseline first and then shadow for live-signal verification.

Rachel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC — evaluation plan and owners (next steps)

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the quick confirmation. Summary & immediate next steps: 

1) Jordan / Sam: upload the 10k holdout set to the Drive folder and confirm masking/anonymization by EOD Fri 2026-10-30.
2) Rachel: run the offline baseline once data is available and share results (metrics + sample failure cases).
3) Marissa: will schedule a 30-min sync for 11/03 to review offline results and confirm whether to proceed to a 1-week shadow run.

I've attached the success criteria spreadsheet and the rubric again for quick reference. If ACME is comfortable with the baseline pass we will target the 11/9 shadow start window.

If anything changes on the timeline, flag me and we can adjust.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
